findings.explanation: The root computation uses inputs under data/ and remodnav/. Following root .gitmodules to data/raw_eyegaze exposes an acquisition-source submodule with an author-local origin. Partial is defensible for the expressly expanded linked-source scope. The assessment correctly avoids claiming that this origin is an input needed by the documented root rerun.

The direct input gitlinks are present at the manifest revisions, but raw_eyegaze/src/lab-eyetracking has a filesystem-only origin. That is a concrete portability/discovery defect, independent of whether public payload URLs currently work. Missing cohort payloads are not used as retrieval-failure evidence.

The root recipe installs the scientific and rendering stack and Docker-Makefile installs the pinned REMoDNaV checkout. The explicitly linked labels component instead runs python from the host with inherited PYTHONPATH. A partially enclosed software environment is supported without attempting execution.

The frozen Git inventory identifies committed code, documentation, configuration and three gitlinks. Intentional omissions in the inspection checkout cannot establish an uncommitted source state. The met judgment concerns version control and is supported.

The manifest records annex symlinks and MD5E size/content keys for the two large image layers and raw eyegaze payloads; the raw-data README describes the separate annex retrieval mechanism. This establishes large-content tracking without needing the bytes.

The 2023 run explicitly records container/image as an extra input, input patterns, img and results_def.tex outputs, and exit 0. The labels run records bash code/compute_all.sh and input/output patterns but no exact environment. Partial follows the actual provenance contrast. A directory output declaration is valid evidence even for unchanged figures; ordinary last-touch commits alone would not refute it.

The root instructions are adequate and explicitly distinguish the old route. However, the same expanded scope used for the environment verdicts includes the labels README: it instructs condor_submit on two absent .submit files and refers to removed preprocessing/detection programs. The tracked producer is instead compute_all.sh, documented in the run history but not reconciled with that README. Native rule 10 caps conflicting documentation and mechanisms at partial.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the declared whole-object scope, preserving root documentation as a strength and identifying the stale linked README commands. A root-only met judgment must be explicitly scoped as such.

findings.explanation: The root has a clear tagged entry point, and the cached tag object resolves to the cited 2023 run. The linked label producer has competing starting points: the README directs users to absent scheduler files, while its result provenance names compute_all.sh. The assessment recognizes linked production elsewhere but omits this documentation-versus-records conflict here; native rule 10 expressly includes must/008.

findings.explanation: Root dataset reads are relative and image-build cleanup paths are internal to the container. The shipped label submission generators really contain an author-specific initial directory and fixed Python executable. Partial is supported; describe these as retained legacy tooling, not the command in the latest recorded labels run.

Root scientific dependencies are enumerated and packaged, but execution also requires separately installed orchestration software and the linked labels process inherits host Python. The linked setup.py lists libraries without capturing that historical host environment. These are specific gaps rather than merely an absent preferred lockfile.

The README names tested platforms and Docker compatibility, yet the adapter assumes an accessible Docker command and usable daemon permissions; the labels scheduler scripts assume an inherited host setup and local working directory. Partial is warranted. The adapter is discoverable through root README version information and the registration, not merely because it exists in the cache.
findings.suggested_correction: For the adapter citation, supplement the movable 1.2.3 tag URL with the frozen source hash or an immutable commit if later established; do not invent a commit.

findings.explanation: Root prerequisites and container dependencies are documented. The label README supplies obsolete scheduler commands instead of a dependency/setup account for the current Python producer. This supports partial; the more actionable deficiency is the stale route as well as the incomplete requirements list.

The recipe, registration and image metadata are committed alongside the analysis. This item asks whether environment specifications are version controlled, not whether every dependency is pinned or every historic environment captured; those shortcomings belong to the separately partial items.

There is a concrete executable build/save procedure and a later recorded image-format update with input/output declarations and exit 0. The Dockerfile history also identifies a tracked environment-setting correction. Accepting these native mechanisms as an update process is reasonable. The duplicate flag is present and matches should/008; the initial archive creation alone would have been insufficient.

The saved image has content-addressed configuration and layers. The inspected adapter hashes the saved configuration and runs the resulting image ID, so the latest label is not evidence of a floating registry dependency on this route. The labels provenance still lacks an exact host environment; partial is supported.

The cited metadata supports publication mechanisms and a public blob locator, but the only stated shortfall is that actual accessibility was not checked. That is not a demonstrated partial violation. The helper itself returns partial when remote checks are skipped, but this conflicts with the conventions requiring not-checked for an access/scope limitation; probe output is not the final authority.
findings.suggested_correction: Use not-checked for the unverified accessibility question, retain the positive published-recipe and annex-URL evidence, and name a permitted future retrieval check as the settling evidence. Flag the helper/status discrepancy; do not imply a failed retrieval.

findings.explanation: The root saved-image acquisition/use route is well documented. The expanded labels computation, which drives partial judgments on must/003, must/006 and must/015, has no corresponding environment acquisition instructions and its README describes removed tools. Whole-object met therefore overstates the documentation coverage and overlooks the native rule about documentation naming absent mechanisms.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial with separate root and linked-label evidence; identify the missing current environment/setup instructions and stale reproduction route.

findings.explanation: Root, labels, raw data, algorithm and validation-data repositories are linked through Git revision identities; annex complements Git for payloads. An unresolved upstream origin does not by itself imply a different version-control system.

The history records occasional root recomputation and image compatibility work, and linked REMoDNaV configures pytest CI. No root CI definition appears in the complete frozen path inventory. That provides positive but incomplete testing coverage, consistent with partial; the CI file establishes configured testing, not an observed successful CI run.

Raw eyegaze and derived labels are separate datasets, REMoDNaV is a separate code component, and root analysis, figures and environment occupy distinct paths. This is relevant modular separation even though not every directory is its own repository.

The recorded numerical/figure computation exited successfully through the Docker adapter; the frozen adapter implements docker run with automatic removal, rather than container reuse. Under the method's equivalent-evidence rule this supports a historical fresh-container test. It does not certify a new execution, a second host, or every upstream producer.

The root creates a disposable Docker container; labels compute_all.sh iterates subject/runs in inherited host Python without creating a fresh environment. The concrete contrast supports partial. Temporary HOME cleanup alone would not establish isolation, but docker run --rm supplies that evidence.

The saved environment was used for analysis and later exercised while converting its representation. These are real historical checks, but the linked CI installs a separate dependency stack and no committed regular study-image test schedule is present. Partial captures the limited existing checks without presenting them as regular full reconstitution testing.

The build record saves the actual image into the object, and the current inventory retains metadata plus annex identities for the blobs. This is an archive mechanism, not only a recipe. Cohort omission of the image bytes limits verification and availability claims, not the existence of the archival representation.

The same executable build/save and later tracked OCI conversion evidence supports the update-process judgment used for must/014. Both duplicate flags are present. The later conversion is important: citing only initial image creation would not meet the native history requirement.

The raw dataset advertises unrestricted access, but the local-only upstream source origin does not establish whether that component is access-restricted. In the assessment's expanded scope, not-checked is an appropriately cautious classification. Neither met nor N/A should be inferred solely from public-facing repositories; a local URL is not evidence of restricted licensing either.

Gitlinks and declarations establish direct and nested dataset/software submodules at recorded revisions. This structural property is met even though a nested origin is not portable and payload reachability remains untested.

The overview describes the object's data/code/figure/manuscript roles, and module declarations expose locations. The actual dependencies on nested validation-data layout and test utilities require reading code, with little guidance about recombination. Partial is supported for the documentation property.

Pinned modules demonstrably support distinct versions, and the root imports remodnav.tests.utils and reads a specific nested dataset layout. These facts show coupling, but the explanation moves from coupling to safe updates being not assured without naming a violated interface or incompatible update. Any dependent workflow has path/API contracts; independent updates do not imply arbitrary revisions are guaranteed compatible.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify the concrete boundary or compatibility contract that fails before retaining partial. Otherwise state that version independence is supported while update compatibility is unverified, and use not-checked if that unresolved property determines the verdict.

findings.explanation: Submodule pins compose data/code; DataLad registration connects the saved image to Docker-Makefile; the recorded root run declares the combined inputs and outputs. These are explicit composition mechanisms and justify met without rerunning them.

The root clone/cd/rerun instructions, module paths and linked annex retrieval instructions provide usable navigation tooling and documentation. The criterion does not require full recombination guidance, so met can coexist with partial on may/002. Stale label reproduction guidance remains the separate actionable defect identified above.

limitations: Inspection only, bounded to manifest e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499, the assigned native method and anonymized assessment. No other assessments, reviews, examples or comparison material were consulted. No network, builds, workflow execution or payload acquisition occurred.

All 31 native response IDs were checked. The checklist pin and response validator pass, but these structural checks do not establish the findings. The supplied response contains no aggregate numeric score or denominator claim to contradict: its native categories contain 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY entries. Unprovided report/probe artifacts were not opened; statements about the original probe run are not independently authenticated.

Missing annex data, images and historical Git blobs limit content and replay verification. A read-only historical Dockerfile diff was unavailable with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; no lazy fetch was allowed. Manifest/source/history hashes checked for 276 available records had no mismatches. This verifies package integrity, not scientific correctness or remote availability.

The review treats explicitly linked computational components as included, consistently with the assigned scope and the assessment's own environment judgments. Root-only reproduction and upstream data regeneration are distinguished; the local upstream source origin is not claimed to block the root rerun.

The supplied Docker adapter is discoverable through the root README tool/version and .datalad/config invocation. Its public URL uses a release tag, so review citations use the frozen relative locator plus SHA256 rather than assert an unknown immutable commit. Historical exit-0 records are evidence of recorded runs, not runs observed in this review.
No observed runtime model identity was available; model_observed remains null. Agreement is an independent evidentiary judgment, not human approval.
